result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings and fixed all of them:

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 05, 87, 138, 140 | The cap only kicked in once the discount went over a higher amount (e.g. 200,000), so discounts between the two were never capped | Always cap the discount |
| 16 | Rounded the discount with `round()` instead of rounding down to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 30 | Threshold was `> 100`, so exactly 100 units got no discount | Changed to `>= 100` |
| 45, 47 | Capped the price before applying the percentage, instead of capping the discount | Work out the discount first, then cap it |
| 134 | Capped the price of the units above the threshold instead of capping the discount | Work out the discount first, then cap it |
| 86 | Labelled "whole" but discounted only the units above the threshold | Discount the full amount (`base * 2 // 100`) |
| 118 | Threshold was 6 instead of 5 | Changed to `>= 5` |
| 135 | Threshold was 13 instead of 12 | Changed to `>= 12` |

To find them, I turned each rule's docstring and the shared rules at the top of the file into a reference calculation. I compared it against all 150 rules over many inputs (up to 20,000 units and prices up to about 1,000,000 won), including the exact threshold and cap values. Before the fix those 12 rules disagreed; after it, none do. That check script is only in a scratch folder, not the project. I changed nothing else.

STATUS: DONE
